MDA is a multi-donor fund which aims at, through technical assistance and capacity strengthening projects, supporting reforms and policy development in accordance with the EU Aquis of Ukraine’s economy, business climate, energy efficiency, and sustainable growth. MDA’s cooperation partners are Ukrainian public sector entities and selected private sector institutions. The MDA has three priority components, namely public administration, corporate governance, and public private dialogue.

MDA är en fond med flera givare som syftar till att, genom tekniskt stöd och kapacitetsstärkande projekt, stödja reformer och policyutveckling i enlighet med EU:s regelverk för Ukrainas ekonomi, företagsklimat, energieffektivitet och hållbar tillväxt. MDA:s samarbetspartners är ukrainska offentliga aktörer och utvalda privata institutioner. MDA har tre prioriterade komponenter: offentlig förvaltning, bolagsstyrning/företagsstyrning (corporate govenance), och offentlig-privat dialog (public private dialogue).

description.narrative:
As of December 2025, the MDA has received a total of EUR 115 million from 17 donors since 2014; Sweden is the third largest donor. 166 projects have been approved for financing under the MDA. During the previous reporting period (July 2024 - June 2025), the MDA Fund had: -54 active projects -4 projects remained on hold due to the ongoing war, as with the previous reporting period,) -6 projects were closed (4 reaching completion and -2 being cancelled because of the war and changing priorities of clients) -21 projects or existing project top-ups were approved.
Selected examples of results (Dec. 2025):
-Ukraine Recovery and Reform Architecture programme (URA) provided technical assistance through Recovery and Reform Support Teams (RST) in seven host institution: Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture, Ministry of Energy, Ministry of Education and Science, State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development, Ministry for Development of Communities and Territories and Recovery and Reform Delivery Office (RDO) under the Prime Minister/Cabinet of Ministers. A new RST at the Ministry of Veterans is in process of being established. 320 national experts positions embedded in above mentioned host institutions, out of which 75% are filled. These experts are active in 30 reform areas. -The RSTs supported ministries in completing EU screening and achieving all 2024 Ukraine Plan targets under MinDevelopment; developed a comprehensive legal roadmap for state owned enterprise (SOE) reform, incl. mechanisms for investor engagement and public-private partnerships; coordinated implementation of the Ukraine Plan across 15 sectors, 69 reforms and 150 implementation benchmarks; supported implementation of processing enterprises' programmes, resulting in 31% increase in total volume of new loans (vs previous year); contributed to the draft of new Labour Code to modernize employment regulation; and Ukraines first comprehensive Law on Vocational Education and Training (VET). -Business Ombudsman Institution (BOI) has since 2015, amongst others received nearly 11,000 business complaints regarding misconduct by state bodies and has successfully closed 7,310 of these cases. -SOEs Management Assistance Reform and Transformation (SMART) Programme provided, amongst others, assistance to the Ministry of Economy of Ukraine on Ownership Policy for State Owned Enterprises and the work on the Law No. 3587 On Amendments to Certain Legislative Acts of Ukraine Relating to Improvement of Corporate Governance in Legal Entities in which the State is a Shareholder/Founder and the reform and adoption of Ukraines first State Ownership Policy (SOP). The adoption of Ownership Policy was EU and International Monetary Funds benchmarks to unlock funding for Ukraine in 2024. It is anticipated that the reform will bring Ukraines SOE governance practices closer to international best practices, including OECD Guidelines on Corporate Governance of SOEs.
